title.narrative: PPDP for Renewable Energy Skills Training and Women Economic Empowerment
PPDP- for Renewable Energy Skills Training and Women Economic Empowerment

description.narrative:
Objective of the intervention
The program overall objective / Impact: The targeted Somali areas (Garowe / Puntland and Mogadishu / Benadir) experience increased socioeconomic growth due to improved access to a) solar electricity, b) local young men and women with requested / demanded technical qualifications, c) enterprises that offer delivery, installation, and maintenance of solar PV and other renewable energy equipment and d) more women are integrated in the economy thereby improved livelihood.
Specific objective/ outcome 1: Electricity companies, other commercial enterprises and public entities have improved access to local labor men and women - with specialized technical skills for exploitation of solar and other renewable energy sources.
Specific objective / outcome 2: Communities, including both businesses and private consumers, have better access to electricity based on solar PV and / or other renewable energy technologies.
Specific objective / outcome 3: More women are integrated in the economy and experience greater economic empowerment and independence.
Output 1: More young men and women have access to demand-driven technical skills training and mentoring in the market segment specializing in electricity production based on solar and other renewable energy sources.
Output 2: More solar PV and other renewable energy systems for electricity production are being installed in commercial enterprises, public entities, and private homes.
Output 3: More women entrepreneurs receive entrepreneurship training and other relevant support to initiate and / or expand their business and increase their revenues.

Nordic International Support Foundation (NIS) har ansökt hos Sida om finansiering på 48 miljoner kronor för att genomföra "PUBLIC PRIVATE DEVELOPMENT PARTNERSHIP (PPDP) for Renewable Energy Skills Training and Women Economic Empowerment in Somalia in Somalia in Somalia under perioden 2022-2025. Programmets övergripande mål / Effekt: De riktade somaliska områdena (Garowe / Puntland och Mogadishu / Benadir) upplever ökad socioekonomisk tillväxt på grund av förbättrad tillgång till a) solenergi, b) lokala unga män och kvinnor med begärda / efterfrågade tekniska kvalifikationer, c) företag som erbjuder leverans, installation och underhåll av solceller och annan utrustning för förnybar energi och d) fler kvinnor integreras i ekonomin och därigenom förbättras försörjningen.
Specifikt mål/resultat 1: Elföretag, andra kommersiella företag och offentliga organ har förbättrat tillgången till lokal arbetskraft – män och kvinnor – med specialiserade tekniska färdigheter för utnyttjande av solenergi och andra förnybara energikällor.
Särskilt mål/resultat 2: Samhällen, inklusive både företag och privata konsumenter, har bättre tillgång till el baserad på solceller och/eller annan teknik för förnybar energi.
Specifikt mål/resultat 3: Fler kvinnor integreras i ekonomin och upplever större ekonomisk egenmakt och oberoende. Den föreslagna interventionen kommer att genomföras i samarbete med utvalda somaliska privata företag, ministeriet för arbetsmarknad och sociala frågor, utbildningsministeriet och ministeriet för energi och vattenresurser. Programmet kommer att föregås av en sex månaders startfas.
Interventionen har en total budget på 48 msek som kommer att finansieras helt av Sverige.

The Nordic International Support Foundation (NIS) has applied to Sida for funding of 48 million SEK to carry out the ‘PUBLIC PRIVATE DEVELOPMENT PARTNERSHIP (PPDP) for Renewable Energy Skills Training and Women Economic Empowerment in Somalia in Somalia during the period 2022-2025. The program overall objective / Impact: The targeted Somali areas (Garowe / Puntland and Mogadishu / Benadir) experience increased socioeconomic growth due to improved access to a) solar electricity, b) local young men and women with requested / demanded technical qualifications, c) enterprises that offer delivery, installation, and maintenance of solar PV and other renewable energy equipment and d) more women are integrated in the economy thereby improved livelihood. Specific objective/ outcome 1: Electricity companies, other commercial enterprises and public entities have improved access to local labor – men and women - with specialized technical skills for exploitation of solar and other renewable energy sources. Specific objective / outcome 2: Communities, including both businesses and private consumers, have better access to electricity based on solar PV and / or other renewable energy technologies. Specific objective / outcome 3: More women are integrated in the economy and experience greater economic empowerment and independence. The proposed intervention will be implemented in partnership with select Somali private companies, the Ministry of Labor and Social Affairs, The Ministry of Educationand the Ministry of Energy and Water Resources. The programme will be preceded by a six month inception phase. The intervention has a total budget of 48 MSEK which will be wholly funded by Sweden.

description.narrative:
This assessment reviews the performance of the Public-Private Development Partnership (PPDP) programme in Somalia as of 2024. The programme aims to foster socio-economic development in targeted regions through improved access to renewable energy, enhanced employability, and expanded income-generating opportunities, particularly for youth and women. Sidas assessment draws on programme reporting, the mid-term evaluation, and field-level monitoring conducted throughout the reporting period.
Progress Toward the Overall Objective
Sida concludes that the programme has contributed to its overarching objective by expanding access to technical training and renewable energy systems. To date, 207 trainees have completed technical training at the Benadir Technical Institute (BTI) and Necsom Technical Institute (NTI), making progress toward the target of 350 graduates. Tracer studies show that 34% of these graduates have secured employment, and among those employed, 88% report increased household income.
However, these figures highlight broader structural constraints in the Somali labour market, particularly in the renewable energy sector. The low employment rate, especially among women, suggests that training gains have not consistently translated into sustainable livelihoods. The programmes overall contribution to economic growth and employment generation remains moderate, mainly influenced by external factors but also delays in implementation have been factors.
Progress Against Specific Outcomes
Outcome 1: Increased Labour Force with Specialised Technical Skills in Renewable Energy The programme has improved enrolment and retention at TVET centres, with enhanced curriculum relevance through private sector engagement, most notably with BECO and NECSOM. However, only 16 of the 207 graduates are women, underscoring significant gender imbalance. Approximately two-thirds of graduates remain unemployed, signalling the need for stronger market linkages and more realistic expectations around immediate job placement.
Outcome 2: Increased Access to Electricity through Renewable Energy Technologies The installation of 651 solar and electrical systems demonstrates the potential of the apprenticeship model and contributes meaningfully to local energy access. However, concerns remain regarding the long-term sustainability and maintenance of these systems post-programme.
Outcome 3: Increased Economic Empowerment and Independence of Women Progress on womens economic empowerment (WEE) has been delayed due to procurement challenges. Key WEE activities only commenced in late 2024, and it is too early to assess their impact. Overall, gender-related objectives remain underachieved.
Implementation Challenges and Programme Responses
The programme faced several challenges:
Delayed Procurement for WEE Activities: Initial bids for female-led solar entrepreneurship training were insufficient. NIS broadened outreach and finalized procurement in December 2024.
Weak Government Coordination: Fragmented coordination between the Federal Government and Puntland State impeded regional engagement. NIS maintained flexible, bilateral communication channels to address this.
Gender and Social Inclusion (GESI) Barriers: Cultural norms and mobility limitations reduced womens participation. In response, NIS developed a tailored GESI strategy and Sida advocated for its integration into TVET sustainability plans.
High Dropout Rates: An 18% dropout rate was reported, mainly due to relocation and inadequate targeting. NIS increased intake and enrolled an additional 121 students in Mogadishu.
Foundational Skills Gaps: Many trainees, especially from IDP communities, struggled with literacy and numeracy. Remedial English and Math classes were introduced to address this.
TVET Centre Sustainability Planning: The development of sustainability plans was delayed. NIS engaged a technical consultant, and the plans were finalized in December 2024.
Conclusions and Recommendations
While the programme has achieved tangible outputs, such as the delivery of technical training and installation of selected energy systems, its transformative impact remains limited. To enhance outcomes in employment, gender equality (both in terms of targeting and mainstreaming), and sustainability, more focused efforts are needed during the remaining implementation period (until June 2025).
Sida acknowledges that the programme has delivered key results in expanding access to energy and vocational training. Nevertheless, challenges remain, particularly with regard to low employment uptake, limited participation of women, and concerns about the durability of results beyond the programmes end.
Persistent structural barriers, including weak governance systems, constrained labour market demand, and socio-cultural norms, continue to impede the full achievement of intended outcomes. These issues, along with operational inefficiencies observed in earlier phases, underscore the need for strategic adjustments.
Based on the programmes 2024 reporting, Sida assesses that most of the intended results are likely to be achieved by the end of the activity period in June 2025, as several of mentioned programme related weaknesses are planned to be addressed during the final six months of programming (Jan - June 2025), although weaknesses are expected to persist in gender-related targeting and mainstreaming.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
